resolutions.researcher_notes: No source found stating the recorded value of 3,400 MMcf/d for the Westcoast/BC Pipeline mainline. Searched: the CER pipeline profile (apps.cer-rec.gc.ca/PPS/en/pipeline-profiles/westcoast-bc-pipeline), which gives only a key-point figure (~1.7 Bcf/d at Huntingdon/FortisBC Lower Mainland), not a system total; and both Enbridge factsheets already opened for this row (BC-Pipeline-Factsheet.pdf and FS_EnergyInfrastructureAssets.pdf, pulled via Wayback due to a live-Enbridge 429), which instead state a PEAK DAY CAPACITY OF 3.6 Bcf/d (3,600 MMcf/d) for the whole BC Pipeline system -- e.g. BC-Pipeline-Factsheet.pdf: 'this pipeline system can move up to 3.6 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day'; FS_EnergyInfrastructureAssets.pdf p.'BC Pipeline': 'Peak day capacity: 3.6 Bcf/d'. This is corroborated by 2 independent Enbridge documents and matches gem.wiki's own current cited capacity for this line (also traced to these same two documents) -- so it is a well-sourced, current figure, but it does NOT match the sheet's recorded 3,400 MMcf/d (a ~200 MMcf/d / ~5.9% gap, well outside rounding tolerance). Not treating this as a rounding-tolerance REFS_ADDED because the found value is a different, round headline figure, not a closer measurement of the same one. Flagging as a likely-stale value rather than fabricating a ref for 3,400: the BC system has had several capacity-adding programs since GEM's number was likely recorded (T-South Reliability +190 MMcf/d ~2021, Spruce Ridge +360 MMcf/d ~2021, Aitken Creek/Chetwynd loops +402 MMcf/d combined, Aspen Point +190 MMcf/d ~2021), consistent with capacity having grown from ~3,400 to 3,600 MMcf/d over that period. Recommend an Update pass revise Capacity to 3,600 MMcf/d / 'Capacity [ref]' citing the BC-Pipeline-Factsheet.pdf and FS_EnergyInfrastructureAssets.pdf URLs above (both url_verifier-clean, non-GEM), rather than leaving 3,400 uncited.

DISAGREEMENT, not a dead end -- flagging rather than citing per standing rule 2/'never propose refs for a different value'. GEM records StartLocation='Kit Carson' (CO) / EndLocation='Sherman' (KS). I opened three independent sources and none supports these as the pipeline's actual termini: (1) the FERC Final EIS (already on this row's Diameter/Length/Fuel refs, federalregister.gov/documents/2004/02/26/E4-412) describes the route running west-to-east through Weld, Morgan, Washington, Yuma, then KIT CARSON county (Colorado, 189.0 mi) and continuing through SHERMAN, Wallace, Logan, Scott, Lane, Finney, Hodgeman, Ford, then Kiowa county (Kansas, 190.8 mi) -- Kit Carson and Sherman are the two counties straddling the CO/KS state line, i.e. roughly the MIDPOINT of the 379.8-mile mainline, not either end; the same EIS places the actual receipt points at the Cheyenne Hub in Weld County, CO and the delivery points in Kiowa County, KS (plus secondary deliveries in Scott/Ford). (2) Kinder Morgan's current operations page (kindermorgan.com/pages/business/gas_pipelines/west/CheyennePlains, fetched this session) states the system 'extends from near the Wyoming-Colorado border to South Central Kansas.' (3) industrialinfo.com (fetched this session) independently names the specific towns: the pipeline is 'originating in the Cheyenne Hub area of northern Colorado, near Greeley, and terminating near Greensburg, Kansas' -- Greensburg is the Kiowa County seat, consistent with the EIS's Kiowa County delivery points. All three sources -- a FERC primary filing, the operator's own current page, and independent trade press -- agree with EACH OTHER and disagree with the recorded Kit Carson/Sherman pair. This reads as a genuine Location correction candidate (StartLocation ~ Cheyenne Hub, Weld County, CO; EndLocation ~ Greensburg, Kiowa County, KS, or the Kiowa County delivery-point cluster) for a separate Update pass, not a ref-sweep fill -- not citing any of the three as support for the recorded Kit Carson/Sherman values. This exact contradiction was already independently identified and flagged as an open validity concern on this row (batches/united-states-gas/staging/deepsweep-west-operating/rows/P0166.json, validity[2], verdict=concern) before this recovery pass; I re-verified two of its three cited sources live this session (kindermorgan.com and industrialinfo.com both returned 200 and matched the quoted claims) rather than merely restating the prior finding.

Filed Date: 10/25/21.' -- Questar Southern Trails Pipeline Company cancelled its ENTIRE FERC Gas Tariff effective November 1, 2021, meaning its FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transportation service ended on that date. ok=true, status=200, name_found=true (Questar Southern Trails Pipeline Company).

resolutions.researcher_notes: CONTRADICTS THE SHEET. GEM records Status=operating. The strongest, most specific primary-source evidence found is FERC Docket RP22-79-000 (Federal Register 2021-23625, Combined Notice of Filings, published 10/29/2021): Questar Southern Trails Pipeline Company cancelled its FERC Gas Tariff First Revised Volume No. 1, effective November 1, 2021 -- i.e. it ended its FERC-jurisdictional interstate transportation tariff altogether. This sits on top of, and is more definitive than, the 2018 NOI (2018-03005) and 2020 extension notice (2020-08973) documenting FERC-authorized abandonment-in-place of the California/Arizona legs (Phase 1 completed June 29, 2019). A Federal Register full-text search for FERC filings by 'MountainWest Southern Trails' (the entity's post-2022 rebrand name per the corporate-successor chain) found none post-cancellation -- the only 2023/2024 'MountainWest'-named FERC filings belong to different entities (MountainWest Overthrust Pipeline LLC; MountainWest Pipeline LLC), not Southern Trails. Separately, the NM/AZ/UT remainder reportedly continues serving Navajo communities (Red Mesa/Kayenta/Tuba City) under NTUA per a Nov 2017 signing (NTUA PDF; lakepowelllife.com), which is consistent with physical gas flow continuing on that segment even after the FERC-jurisdictional tariff was cancelled (e.g. if NTUA now operates it outside FERC's interstate jurisdiction) -- but no source directly confirms current status in FERC's own terms post-cancellation. Given the shard's class_out options have no 'stale/contested' category and the strongest primary-source evidence directly contradicts an unqualified 'operating' status for the FERC-jurisdictional pipeline as recorded, marking UNRESOLVED rather than falsely emitting REFS_ADDED. RECOMMEND ROUTING: Status likely needs a ResearcherNotes flag distinguishing 'the NM/AZ/UT segment may still flow gas under NTUA' from 'the FERC-jurisdictional Southern Trails Pipeline Company tariff/interstate service ended 11/1/2021' -- this is a materially different, more specific and more recent finding than the 2018/2020 partial-abandonment dockets alone would suggest.
